origin: the killed-dispatch anchor gap — a review dispatched at a dying close attempt and closed as bookkeeping occupied the only slot, and the classifier took its incorporated status as proof a review had run: a skip-happy user could then conclude with no review ever reading the document; this walk pins the reclassification — a row with no report is not a review, so the close still owes the mandatory pass
conduct: The user settled how card payments at checkout should work in earlier sessions and is returning only to close the discussion out. Everything they cared about is decided and documented — capture confirmed by gateway webhooks, hosted fields keeping card data off their servers, a pinned retry policy — and they add nothing new: picking the session back up they confirm in a sentence that nothing has changed for them, say that covers it, and ask to wrap up. On the way out they are agreeable to required steps — a mandatory review or the conclusion gets a yes — but they decline optional extras: another final review is skipped when offered, offers of new threads are declined. They never introduce new material.

stubs.discussion-review-clean: when the engine records a dispatch of kind review — write the content to the path the dispatch response returned
